Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-10

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everybody, welcome thanks for hopping on, uh quick check, can folks hear me?
[00:04] Lena Torres: yes, loud and clear. thanks Maya.
[00:07] Ethan Park: good afternoon all, Ethan on the call from Redwood infra team.
[00:12] Rajesh Patel: Rajesh here. we'll jump right in.
[00:15] Maya Chen: okay great. goal for today is to walk through the remaining security gating items for the pilot — specifically SSO, audit logs, retention, and a quick sanity on SOC2 related asks. should be 30 to 45.
[00:26] Chris O'Neill: that works. we've had a couple internal askers about whether logs can be streamed to our SIEM and how long retention will be.
[00:33] Ethan Park: yep we can do streaming, we've got a couple options — direct HTTPS push to your SIEM, write to S3 and fwd with lambda, or syslog via a collector. we'll show a sample schema. note: the "audit_log" object has event_type, actor_id, request_id, model, token_count etc but sometimes the auto transcriber writes it as "odel" in our notes, sorry.
[00:53] Rajesh Patel: are you encrypting logs at rest and in transit? and can we supply our K M S?
[00:58] Ethan Park: yes, logs are TLS encrypted in transit; at rest we support customer-managed keys on Dedicated and Private — Redwood Privat and Redwood Dedicate sometimes shows up in the notes but the product names are Redwood Dedicated and Redwood Private. for hosted we use server-managed keys but can do envelope encryption on request.
[01:15] Lena Torres: for the pilot we must prove both SSO and audit streaming before going to security sign-off. timeline for SSO in staging?
[01:22] Maya Chen: how do you want to do SSO, Okta SAML or OIDC? we typically recommend SAML for SSO with SCIM user provisioning but OIDC is simpler for token flows.
[01:33] Rajesh Patel: we run Okta already — we prefer SAML + SCIM. also want to ensure session timeout policies can be enforced.
[01:40] Ethan Park: ok we have a config guide for Okta SAML + SCIM, will share a test app manifest. one thing to note is session handling for streaming generates a short-lived API token on our side; we respect your session TTL via SAML assertion mapping, though the transcriber often mangles that to "session T T L" in notes.
[01:58] Chris O'Neill: for audit logs, what fields come through? do you include prompt text? we need to mask PII by default.
[02:06] Ethan Park: you can toggle payload granularity. default pilot mode logs metadata only (request_id, model, timestamps, user_id hash, tokens). full prompt text is optional — it's off by default for enterprise pilots if you pick the privacy-safe template. we also support server-side redaction: simple pattern-based and custom redaction hooks. note: the phrase "K V cache" appears in infra notes sometimes as "K V cash" — ignore that.
[02:34] Rajesh Patel: good. what about retention? our policy is 90 days for logs and 30 days for any PII. can your automatic purge be configured?
[02:42] Ethan Park: yes retention is configurable per workspace. default hosted is 180 days, Dedicated/Private you can set exact retention and lifecycle rules. automatic purge can be scheduled, and we emit deletion events so you can track them in your SIEM.
[02:57] Maya Chen: Rajesh, is SOC2 a hard stop for you or just preferred?
[03:01] Rajesh Patel: it's required for production — must have evidence of controls, and we need to see mapping for the Redwood platform controls to our SOC2 control matrix.
[03:09] Maya Chen: okay we'll provide the control mapping and evidence locations. Ethan, we should capture which artifacts we can hand over (audit logs, config change history, key rotation records).
[03:19] Ethan Park: yes, we keep key rotation metadata and audit trails of config changes in the control plane. for Dedicated and Private you can also enable longer retention for audit artifacts. note that platform-level logs are separate from request-level audit logs.
[03:33] Chris O'Neill: any blockers we should know about? either technical or time.
[03:36] Ethan Park: technical blockers: none obvious. we need your Okta test tenant and a service account for SCIM provisioning. we also want to run a log throughput test — samples show 20 QPS of audit events per 1k users during heavy inference, but your pattern might differ.
[03:52] Lena Torres: we can provision Okta staging but will need a short doc of the exact SAML attributes to map.
[03:58] Maya Chen: we'll share that in the SSO guide. I'll put it in the follow-up email.
[04:03] Rajesh Patel: about encryption keys — for Dedicated we would want to bring our own key. is there a K M S connector for AWS KMS or HSM?
[04:11] Ethan Park: yes AWS KMS, Google KMS, and HSM integrations for Private. on hosted we support envelope keys but not customer HSM by default. again some transcriptions show "H S M" spaced out.
[04:22] Chris O'Neill: what about RBAC? can we limit which roles can request model access or view logs?
[04:27] Ethan Park: yes RBAC is per workspace, with built-in roles and custom roles you can define. we also provide token-level scopes, and audit logs capture policy changes.
[04:36] Lena Torres: great. could you show me the sample audit payload?
[04:39] Ethan Park: sure, I'll paste a trimmed example here in chat after the call, but briefly: {"event_type": "generation.request", "ts": "2026-12-10T14:59:xxZ", "req_id": "r-...", "user_hash": "h-...", "model": "redwood-v2", "verb": "create", "token_count": 48} — full schema will be in the doc.
[05:00] Maya Chen: quick note about compliance: we'll include a mapping doc that highlights gaps and mitigations. often customers want a checklist: SSO configured, audit streaming validated, retention rules set, SOC2 evidence export tested.
[05:15] Rajesh Patel: for the SOC2 export, is there a packaged export or do we need to pull artifacts from multiple places?
[05:20] Ethan Park: we offer a compressed artifact export for Dedicated and Private deployments — it bundles logs, config history, and rotation events. for hosted, we can generate an export but there are limits on the retention window.
[05:33] Chris O'Neill: any pricing delta for Dedicated or Private due to these integrations?
[05:37] Maya Chen: yes there is a pricing delta for Dedicated/Private to cover reserved capacity and increased storage/retention. I'll include a delta in the follow-up doc.
[05:45] Lena Torres: timeline questions — if we get staging Okta to you by next Tuesday, how fast can you enable SSO in our staging env?
[05:52] Ethan Park: once we have the Okta test app and SCIM creds, we can enable SSO in staging within 48 hours and run a provisioning test.
[05:59] Maya Chen: good. on the audit log side we'll need to coordinate the sample stream. we propose a small bench test next week to validate throughput and retention.
[06:09] Rajesh Patel: one more on privacy — do you perform any model fine-tuning with customer data in the hosted environment? are requests ever used to improve shared models?
[06:18] Ethan Park: for pilots and enterprise we can guarantee no training on customer data unless explicitly contracted. hosted default is to not train on customer content; we can put that in the DPA.
[06:28] Chris O'Neill: ok thanks.
[06:30] Maya Chen: let's capture next steps and owners now.
[06:32] Ethan Park: I'll take the audit-log sample and schema.
[06:35] Maya Chen: I'll send SOC2 mapping and the staging SSO checklist plus pricing delta.
[06:38] Lena Torres: i'll provision an Okta staging app and invite Ethan and Maya to it.
[06:42] Rajesh Patel: i'll review the SOC2 scoping doc when it's shared and then route to our compliance team.
[06:46] Chris O'Neill: i'll coordinate the bench test schedule with Ethan.
[06:49] Maya Chen: perfect. any open questions?
[06:51] Lena Torres: none from me, this was helpful.
[06:54] Rajesh Patel: none. thanks folks.
[06:56] Maya Chen: great thanks all. we'll follow up with the items discussed and set the bench test in the calendar. talk soon.

End of transcript.
